title: pMarineViewer Button Posts
prompt:
This viewer button is supposed to deploy the vehicle, but clicking it does not make the helm run. Correct the configuration conceptually and explain what should be checked in uXMS:

```text
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true
}
```

chatgpt.text:
ht for a couple of seconds

The button is probably posting the wrong type/value or posting only one of the variables needed for the helm to leave standby.

Conceptually, a pMarineViewer button should post MOOS variables exactly as the helm behavior conditions expect:

ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true
  button_two = MANUAL # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true
  button_three = RETURN # RETURN=true
}

But for actual deployment, most MOOS-IvP missions need both:

DEPLOY = true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE = false

So the deploy button is usually something like:

button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false

or, in some mission styles:

button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true
button_two = AUTO # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false

The key idea is that DEPLOY=true may satisfy the behavior condition, but the helm may still not run autonomous behaviors if MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE remains true.

Check these in uXMS:

Bash
uXMS DEPLOY MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE IVPHELM_STATE DESIRED_HEADING DESIRED_SPEED

You want to see:

DEPLOY                = true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE  = false
IVPHELM_STATE         = DRIVE

If clicking the button changes nothing, the issue is in the pMarineViewer config or you are not running the generated .moos file you edited. If DEPLOY=true appears but MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=true remains, the helm is still manually overridden. If both variables look correct but the helm does not drive, inspect the .bhv conditions and helm status with uHelmScope.

Also make sure the button syntax is in the actual pMarineViewer block of the running target file, not only in a stale meta_*.moos template. If you edited the template, regenerate with nsplug before relaunching.

Claude responded: The Problem
The Problem

The button is only posting DEPLOY=true, but the MOOS-IvP helm won't actually run on that alone. The helm requires three conditions to be satisfied simultaneously:

DEPLOY=true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false
RETURN=false (commonly also required)

Your config only sets one of them, so the helm stays idle.

Corrected Configuration
text
ProcessConfig = pMarineViewer
{
  button_one = DEPLOY # DEPLOY=true # MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE=false # RETURN=false
}

Each #-separated token is an additional MOOS variable posting. All three get published atomically when the button is clicked.

What to Check in uXMS

Open uXMS and filter for these variables to verify their state:

Variable	Expected value when deployed
DEPLOY	true
MOOS_MANUAL_OVERRIDE	false
RETURN	false
IVPHELM_STATE	Drive (confirms helm is actually running behaviors)
IVPHELM_ALLSTOP	clear (any other value means the helm is holding itself back)

The key diagnostic is IVPHELM_STATE — if it reads Park even after clicking Deploy, that tells you one of the interlock variables is still in the wrong state. IVPHELM_ALLSTOP will tell you why it's parked if that's the case.
